The word "board" has several distinct meanings. Most of them share a common thread: something flat, hard, and rectangular — either a physical object or, in some cases, a group of people or a concept built around that image of a flat surface. Once you feel that underlying idea, the different meanings start to connect naturally.
1. A Flat Piece of Hard Material

The most basic and original meaning: a flat, thin, usually rectangular piece of a hard material — most often wood. Think of the planks used to build a floor, a fence, a bookshelf, or a wall. Each of those planks is a board.

  • The carpenter nailed the boards together to make a door.
  • She pried a loose board off the old floor.
  • They covered the broken window with a board.

Boards in this sense are the building blocks of construction. They're cut flat and smooth from larger pieces of wood or similar material.

This meaning appears in many compound words:

  • Floorboard — one of the boards that makes up a floor
  • Surfboard — a flat board you stand on to ride ocean waves
  • Skateboard — a flat board mounted on wheels, used for skating
  • Snowboard — a wide, flat board you strap to your feet to glide down snow
  • Diving board — a flat, springy board you jump off at a swimming pool
  • Ironing board — a narrow padded board you use to iron clothes flat
  • Cutting board / chopping board — a flat kitchen board on which you cut vegetables, meat, or bread
  • Circuit board / motherboard — a flat board inside computers and electronics on which tiny components are attached and connected
2. A Flat Surface for Displaying or Writing Information

A board can be any flat surface designed for people to look at — to read information, see announcements, or check scores. These are boards because they are literally flat panels, but their purpose is communication.

  • The teacher wrote the equation on the board. (a whiteboard or blackboard at the front of a classroom)
  • Check the notice board outside the office for updates.
  • The score is up on the scoreboard — we're winning!

Types in this category:

  • Blackboard / chalkboard — a dark board you write on with chalk, common in older classrooms
  • Whiteboard — a smooth white board you write on with dry-erase markers; easily wiped clean
  • Notice board / bulletin board — a board where you pin papers, announcements, or messages
  • Scoreboard — a large board (or screen) showing the score in a sports match
  • Billboard — a very large outdoor board used for advertising, typically seen along roads
3. A Flat Surface for Playing a Game

Many games are played on a flat, marked surface called a board. This is the foundation of the phrase "board game."

  • Set up the board before we start playing chess.
  • Roll the dice and move your piece forward on the board.
  • He missed the dartboard completely and hit the wall.

Types:

  • Chessboard — the 8×8 checked board used in chess
  • Game board — the general term for the flat surface used in any board game (Monopoly, Ludo, Scrabble, etc.)
  • Dartboard — the circular, numbered board you throw darts at

The phrase "board game" itself comes directly from this meaning — any game whose play is organized around a flat board.
4. A Group of People Who Run an Organization

This meaning is completely different from all the physical ones above. Here, "board" refers to a group of people officially in charge of managing or governing a company, school, hospital, charity, or other institution.

The idea comes from the image of important people sitting around a large flat table (a "board table" or "boardroom table") to make decisions together. Over time, the word came to describe the group itself, not just the table.

  • The board decided to hire a new director.
  • The company's board of directors meets four times a year.
  • She was elected to the board of the local hospital.
  • The school board voted to close two underperforming schools.

Common versions of this:

  • Board of directors — the governing group of a company or corporation
  • Board of trustees — the governing body of a university, museum, charity, or nonprofit
  • School board — the group of officials that oversees a public school system in a district
  • Board of governors — the ruling body of certain institutions or regions

When people say "the board approved the plan" or "take it to the board," they mean this powerful committee of officials.
5. Meals Provided Regularly (Often With Accommodation)

"Board" can also mean regular meals — specifically meals provided as part of a living or accommodation arrangement. You'll most often see this in the phrase "room and board," which means a place to sleep plus meals.

  • The monthly rent includes room and board. (= a bedroom + three meals a day)
  • University students pay a separate fee for board in the dining hall.
  • She looked for a job that offered free room and board.

This meaning is also where the word boarding school comes from — a school where students both live and eat (they receive "board," meaning regular meals). A student who lives at such a school is called a boarder.

Two related terms used mainly in hotels and travel:

  • Full board — accommodation with all three meals (breakfast, lunch, and dinner) included
  • Half board — accommodation with only two meals included (usually breakfast and dinner)
6. The Stage in a Theatre

In the world of theatre and performance, "the boards" (almost always plural) refers to the wooden stage on which actors perform. It comes from the fact that theatre stages were traditionally made of wooden boards.

  • She finally got to tread the boards after years of acting classes. (= perform on a real stage)
  • He's been on the boards since he was a teenager. (= he's been a professional actor for years)

The idiom "tread the boards" means to work as an actor or to perform in a play. It's a classic, somewhat poetic expression.
7. The Walls Around an Ice Hockey Rink

In ice hockey, "the boards" refers to the low, solid walls that enclose the rink and stop the puck — and flying players — from leaving the playing surface.

  • The defender slammed his opponent into the boards.
  • The puck bounced off the boards and slid behind the goal.

As with the theatre meaning, this is nearly always used in the plural.
8. Stiff, Thick Material (Used in Books and Packaging)

In bookbinding and manufacturing, "board" refers to thick, stiff cardboard-like material used to make book covers, boxes, and other firm surfaces.

  • The hardcover book has cloth-covered boards. (= the hard covers are made from rigid board material)
  • The product was packed between two pieces of board to protect it.

The word "cardboard" itself is built from this: it's a card-like, stiff board material. Similarly, "pasteboard" and "hardboard" are types of stiff board used in manufacturing and construction.
Common Phrases and Idioms

Understanding a word fully means knowing how it appears in everyday expressions. Here are the most important ones with "board":

  • On board — (1) physically on a ship, aircraft, or train: "All passengers are now on board." (2) figuratively, in agreement with a plan or idea: "Is everyone on board with the new strategy?"
  • Across the board — affecting all people or things equally, without exception: "The company announced salary increases across the board."
  • Back to the drawing board — to start completely over because something didn't work: "The design failed the tests, so it's back to the drawing board."
  • Above board — completely honest, open, and legal, with nothing hidden or secret: "All our business dealings are completely above board." (The image is of a card player keeping their hands visibly above the table — the board — to show they aren't cheating.)
  • Take on board — to accept, consider, or absorb information, advice, or a new idea (especially common in British English): "She took the criticism on board and rewrote the report."
  • Sweep the board — to win every prize, award, or competition in a situation: "Their film swept the board at the awards ceremony."
  • Go overboard — to do something to an excessive or extreme degree: "Don't go overboard with the decorations — keep it simple."
The Full Picture

Here is every meaning of "board" as a noun, clearly summarized:

  1. A flat plank or sheet of hard material (wooden boards, floorboards)
  2. A flat surface for displaying or writing information (whiteboard, scoreboard, noticeboard)
  3. A flat surface for playing a game (chessboard, dartboard, game boards)
  4. A group of people who govern or run an organization (board of directors, school board)
  5. Regular meals provided as part of accommodation (room and board, full board)
  6. The theatrical stage ("the boards," tread the boards)
  7. The walls around an ice hockey rink ("the boards")
  8. Stiff cardboard-like material used in manufacturing and bookbinding

The single most useful mental image to carry with you: a flat, firm, rectangular surface. Whether it's a plank of wood, a classroom whiteboard, a chess game board, or — stretched into the abstract — the "table" around which powerful people sit to make decisions, the idea of something flat and solid runs through almost every use of this word.
